content: Common take-home-assignment failure modes: (1) scope creep -- building tangential/impressive-looking features instead of nailing the core requirement; rule of thumb is 'does this improve the stated requirement, or is it just cool' -- if tangential, cut it; (2) execution failures -- the single most common rejection cause is the reviewer being unable to run the project at all (missing deps, broken build, wrong start command), so 'make it run, then make it good' before adding features; (3) using an unfamiliar tech stack on top of an already time-boxed task compounds risk -- stick to tools you already know well for anything not central to the assessment. For a deployed-URL requirement specifically, this generalizes to: get a bare-bones deploy live on day 1, not day 4, so deployment/CI problems surface while there's still time to fix them.
